# Settings reference

Every key a project file (`hxex.toml`) accepts, table by table, with its type, its default and what it does. `hxex init --format FORMAT` writes a file with these defaults and shorter comments; [The project file](project-file.md) explains how the file works.

Conventions: a key left out keeps its default. TOML has no null, so `false` stands for *unset* where a setting can be unset (an optional stage, a limit); a switch set to `false` is off. Times are in seconds, written as a number or as text with a unit (`"5 min"`, `"20 h"`). Relative paths are relative to the project file. *required* means the table needs the key. A heading in double brackets (`[[input.runs]]`) is for something there can be several of: write the heading once for each, each followed by its own settings (with only one, single brackets work too).

## Top level

Top-level keys, before the first table.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | text | required | the project's name (text without a colon, `:`); prefixes every spectrum id |
| `threads` | integer | unset | CPU threads for the command (unset: PyTorch's default, the physical cores); about half the physical cores was fastest on a 24-core machine |

## `[input]`

What to read. Which keys apply depends on the format (the Formats column): folder = the folder formats (specexport, hxexpress, pooled), scan = the scan formats (mzml, thermo), all = every format. See [Input formats](inputs.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Formats | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | required | all | specexport, hxexpress, pooled (folder formats), mzml or thermo (scan formats) |
| `data_dir` | path | unset | folder | the folder to read (needed for the folder formats) |
| `samples` | list | unset | folder | only these samples (unset: all) |
| `peptide_ranges` | list | unset | folder | only these peptides, by their residues: "1-10" selects the peptide from residue 1 to 10 ("0001-0010" is the same); unset: all |
| `peptide_region` | list | unset | folder | [first, last]: only peptides wholly within these residues; with peptide_ranges too, a peptide that matches either; unset: all |
| `sample` | text | `""` | pooled | the sample name given to the entries of a pooled folder |
| `record_paths` | text | `"path"` | all | how the files read are recorded in the bundle: "path" (as given), "name" (file names only), or for the scan formats "relative" (to data_root) |
| `time_scale` | text | `"seconds"` | all | "seconds" (real times) or "order" (the times only order the points: uptake drawn by index, kinetics and protection analyses refuse) |
| `peptides` | path | unset | all | scan formats: the peptide table (CSV), needed; each row is read from the runs of its sample (every run when it has none); folder formats: a table of the files instead of finding them by name |
| `runs` | list | `[]` | scan | one [[input.runs]] table per file (below) |
| `parents` | true/false | `true` | scan | read each peptide itself; false reads only its fragments (needs [[input.fragments]]) |
| `target` | table | {} | scan | how the peptides' scans are chosen: the [input.target] table (below) |
| `fragments` | list | `[]` | scan | fragment ions of every peptide: [[input.fragments]] tables (below) |
| `scans` | table | (table) | scan | how scans become spectra: the [input.scans] table (below) |
| `data_root` | path | `"."` | scan | relative run paths are taken from here |
| `thermo_dir` | path | unset | thermo | the folder of Thermo's RawFileReader DLLs (else the HXEX_THERMO_DIR environment variable) |
| `retention_times` | path | unset | all | a table of retention times in minutes (columns rt and sample, start_seq, end_seq, peptide, charge) |
| `spectra` | path | unset | all | take the raw spectra stored by an earlier run (a bundle or a spectra file) instead of reading the input |
| `exclude` | list | `[]` | all | spectra left out before fitting: [[input.exclude]] rules (below) |

## `[input.target]`

Scan formats: how the scans of the peptides themselves are chosen.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms_level` | integer | `1` | MS level of the peptides' scans |
| `activation` | text | unset | activation of the scans (e.g. "HCD"; unset: any) |
| `precursor_mz` | number | unset | m/z of the scans' precursor (unset: any) |
| `precursor_charge` | integer | unset | charge of the scans' precursor (unset: any) |
| `rt_window` | list | unset | [start, end] in s of scan time: the scans used in runs with a fixed time (a peptide's rt_start, rt_end columns, in minutes, take its place) |
| `filter_contains` | text | unset | text the scan filter must contain |
| `filter_excludes` | text | unset | text the scan filter must not contain (e.g. "sid") |
| `parent_mz` | list | unset | [low, high] m/z the scans' parent isolation must overlap (unset: any) |
| `preactivation` | text | unset | MS3: the activation before the last stage ("none" for none) |

## `[[input.runs]]`

Scan formats: one table per file. A file with a time is one time point, a file with a role is a control, and a file with neither is a kinetics run whose every scan has its own time. Two clocks: the scan time (acquisition clock) and the exchange clock, scan time + time_offset.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | text or path | required | the file (relative paths from data_root) |
| `sample` | text | required | the sample the file belongs to |
| `rep` | integer | `1` | replicate number (1 or more); left out, the runs of one sample at one time or control role are numbered in the order listed |
| `time` | number | unset | labelling time of the whole file (s, or text with a unit: "60 s", "5 min"); leave it out when each scan has its own time (kinetics) |
| `time_offset` | number | `0.0` | s: the exchange clock is the scan time plus this (when exchange began relative to acquisition) |
| `usable_from` | number | unset | s of scan time: this file's scans before it are left out (it does not move the time axis; time_offset does) |
| `activation` | text | `"target"` | "target" keeps the targets' condition; a value replaces it for this file only, false removes it |
| `precursor_mz` | number or text | `"target"` | as activation: "target", a value, or false (any) |
| `precursor_charge` | integer or text | `"target"` | as activation: "target", a charge, or false (any; for a file that records a wrong precursor charge) |
| `filter_contains` | text | `"target"` | as activation: "target", a text, or false |
| `filter_excludes` | text | `"target"` | as activation: "target", a text, or false (e.g. a control file acquired with in-source activation throughout) |
| `role` | text | `""` | "undeut" or "fulldeut": a control file, its scans summed into one spectrum without a time (with time as well: a time point that also serves as the control) |

## `[[input.fragments]]`

Scan formats: fragment ions made from every peptide of the table. Repeat the table for other conditions (e.g. with and without in-source activation).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ions` | text | required | space-separated TYPE:LENGTHS:CHARGES items ("c-1:ALL z-dot:2-6,9"); LENGTHS and CHARGES are ALL (the default) or numbers and ranges; types such as c, c-1, z-dot, y-NH3, M (the peptide itself) |
| `label` | text | unset | names the condition in tables and figures ("gentle") |
| `ms_level` | integer | `2` | 2, or 3 for MS3 scans |
| `activation` | text | unset | activation of the last stage |
| `preactivation` | text | unset | MS3: the activation before the last stage ("none" for none) |
| `parent_mz` | list or text | `"parent"` | "parent" (scans whose isolation overlaps the peptide's m/z range), [low, high] in m/z, or false (any parent) |
| `precursor_mz` | number | unset | m/z of the scans' precursor (unset: any) |
| `precursor_charge` | integer or text | `"parent"` | "parent", a charge, or false (any) |
| `filter_contains` | text | unset | text the scan filter must contain |
| `filter_excludes` | text | unset | text the scan filter must not contain |
| `rt_window` | list | unset | [start, end] in s of scan time, for runs with a fixed time (a peptide's rt_start, rt_end columns take its place) |
| `limit_charge` | true/false | `true` | ALL charges run from 1 to the parent's charge - 1 (false: to the parent's charge); charges written out are used as given |

## `[[input.exclude]]`

Spectra left out before fitting: they are stored with the raw spectra but not picked or fitted, and the bundle records them. A spectrum is excluded when it matches every key one rule names; repeat the heading for each rule. See [Excluding spectra](excluding-spectra.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sample` | text | unset | the sample |
| `peptide_range` | text | unset | the peptide, by its residues ("45-60" is "0045-0060") |
| `charge` | integer | unset | the charge state |
| `time` | number or text | unset | a time point (s, or text with a unit: "30 s"); a control has no time |
| `role` | text | unset | "undeut" or "fulldeut": the controls |
| `rep` | integer | unset | the replicate |
| `file` | text | unset | the data file's name: a run's mzML or raw file, an HX-Express spreadsheet, or a SpecExport spectrum file |
| `spectrum_id` | text | unset | one spectrum, by its id (spectra.csv) |
| `note` | text | `""` | why: kept with the record, and shown by hxex check and hxex info |

## `[input.scans]`

Scan formats: how scans become spectra (hxex.io.MzmlConfig).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | text | `"each"` | one spectrum per scan ("each"), per "every" scans summed, or per time window ("windows"); runs with a fixed time sum all their scans |
| `every` | integer | `1` | scans summed per spectrum with group = "every" |
| `windows` | list | `[]` | with group = "windows": [[start, end], ...] in s of scan time |
| `min_time` | number | unset | s of scan time: leave out every run's scans before it (false: none); not the exchange-clock min_time of [analysis.fragments] |
| `max_spectra` | integer | unset | most spectra per target in a run without a fixed time, spread over log time (false: all) |
| `mz_margin` | number | `2.0` | m/z kept on either side of a target's predicted bins |
| `sum_ppm` | number | `10.0` | centroided peaks closer than this (ppm) are summed |
| `gap_factor` | number | `3.0` | profile scans: a point spacing this many times its neighbours' is a stretch the instrument left out |
| `precursor_tol` | number | `1.0` | m/z tolerance matching a scan's precursor to a target's |
| `find_peak` | true/false | `false` | LC-MS runs with a fixed time: find each peptide's elution peak near its rt (peptide table, minutes) and sum that peak's scans; rows with rt_start, rt_end keep them |
| `peak_search` | number | `30.0` | s either side of a peptide's rt that its peak is looked for in |
| `peak_smoothing` | number | unset | s: the chromatogram's running mean (false: half the run's typical peak width, measured) |
| `peak_width` | number | `0.5` | the window: the apex +- this many peak widths at half maximum |

## `[output]`

Where results go. The bundle and the folders named after it (<bundle>_tables, <bundle>_figures, <bundle>_analysis_<reference>, and the generations <bundle>.1, ...) belong to *hxex*: a later run replaces or renames them.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | path | unset | name of the folder (or .zip archive, a name ending in .zip) that `hxex run` creates for the results (the bundle); it must not exist yet unless overwrite or keep_previous is set |
| `overwrite` | true/false | `false` | replace an existing bundle (its review is carried over) and its tables (its figures and analyses stay until redrawn) |
| `keep_previous` | true/false | `false` | move the existing bundle, tables and figures to the next generation (results.1, ...) first |
| `keep_spectra` | true/false | `true` | store the raw spectra in the bundle (needed to rerun from it) |
| `tables` | path or true/false | `true` | CSV tables: true beside the bundle (<bundle>_tables), a directory, or false |
| `notes` | text | `""` | free text kept in the bundle's manifest |

## `[run]`

Run settings (hxex.run.RunConfig); times are in s, as the measurement times. The bootstrap, the population test, and the controls are stages that their table turns on: uncomment the commented-out run.bootstrap, run.population_test, or run.controls table below to use it; a stage's "name = false" turns it off.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `envelope_fallback_time` | number | unset | s: spectra at this time are the envelope references when a series' undeuterated controls are missing or poor (false: none) |
| `n_max_factor` | number | `1.2` | n (exchangeable sites) may be up to this times the amide count |
| `drop_no_signal` | true/false | `true` | drop spectra the picker found no signal in (empty ones always are) |
| `memory_budget_bytes` | integer | unset | memory of one chunk of the fit, bytes (false: automatic) |
| `max_chunk` | integer | unset | most measurements in one chunk (false: no cap) |

## `[run.picker]`

Peak picking: the spectra become sticks at the predicted isotope positions (hxex.picking.PickerConfig; docs/PEAK_PICKING.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pick` | text | `"peak"` | what a bin takes: "peak" (the tallest peak whose apex is in the window) or "window_max" (the tallest point in the window, as pyHXExpress) |
| `measure` | text | `"auto"` | the value a picked peak gives its bin: "auto" (areas when the run's undeuterated controls show weak peaks wider than tall ones, as on the Q-TOF data tested; heights otherwise, as on an Orbitrap; hxex info says which), "height" (as pyHXExpress) or "area" |
| `area_fwhm` | number | `1.5` | with areas: how far either side of a peak's apex its area is taken, in peak widths at half maximum (measured from the run) |
| `resolution_ppm` | number | `50.0` | half-width (ppm) of the window a peak is picked in around its predicted m/z (never above half the isotope spacing); not a resolving power |
| `zero_filling` | integer | `4` | bins picked after the last one above the noise threshold |
| `noise_threshold` | number | unset | absolute intensity below which a point is noise (false: noise_percent of the tallest point instead) |
| `noise_percent` | number | `1.0` | noise threshold as percent of the spectrum's tallest point |
| `env_threshold` | number | `0.1` | fraction of the tallest bin at which the envelope width is measured |
| `nterm_subtract` | integer | `1` | N-terminal residues without an exchanging amide (the amide count bounds the bins); none after an acetylated N-terminus (Ac-), whose residue 1 keeps its amide |
| `shoulder_min_points` | integer | `10` | with pick = "window_max": points in a window from which a maximum at its edge counts as a neighbour's shoulder (bin 0) |
| `ladder` | text | `"composition"` | bin positions: "composition" (isotope clusters of the composition) or "exms" (pyHXExpress's fixed steps) |
| `resolving_power` | number or text | unset | with pick = "window_max" only: window from the instrument instead of resolution_ppm: R quoted at resolving_power_mz, or "recorded" (each spectrum's value from Thermo raw files; hxex check shows them); false: the resolution_ppm window (always so with pick = "peak") |
| `resolving_power_mz` | number | `200.0` | m/z the resolving power is quoted at (Thermo: 200; 400 on the first Orbitrap generation) |
| `resolving_power_exponent` | number | `0.5` | R falls as (m0/m)^e: 0.5 Orbitrap, 0 TOF, 1 FT-ICR |
| `window_fwhm` | number | `1.0` | half-width as a multiple of the peak width at half maximum, m/R(m); never below mass_accuracy_ppm, never above half the isotope spacing |
| `mass_accuracy_ppm` | number | `10.0` | floor (ppm) of the resolving-power window |
| `off_mz_sd` | number | `6.0` | off_mz: a series whose undeuterated controls put its envelope further than this many times the run's scatter from the run's calibration (at least 3 ppm; peptide ions only; false: not checked) |
| `recentre` | true/false | `true` | move the windows of an off_mz series onto its undeuterated envelope's peaks (false: flag only) |

## `[run.picker.amide_rules]`

Per fragment ion type, whether it keeps the amide N-H at its cleavage site, e.g. "y-NH3" = false. Empty: the ion type's composition decides (c, x, y keep it; a, b, z do not).


## `[run.fit]`

The fit of k_min to k_max populations to every spectrum, the number chosen by the criterion; with k_min and k_max equal, that number only (hxex.fit.FitConfig).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k_min` | integer | `1` | fewest populations tried (must be 1 with screen; the controls are also fitted at K = 1 for the back-exchange correction, whatever k_min) |
| `k_max` | integer | `3` | most populations tried (equal to k_min: that number only, no choice) |
| `criterion` | text | `"bic"` | "bic" or "aic": chooses K among those tried |
| `min_population` | number | `0.05` | a K whose smallest population is below this is rejected (0: off); [analysis.filters] and [analysis.choice] have their own |
| `n_restarts` | integer | `6` | starting points per K |
| `adam_steps` | integer | `400` | Adam steps per restart |
| `k1_adam_steps` | integer | unset | Adam steps of the K=1 fit only (false: adam_steps); 200 is enough and faster |
| `lbfgs_steps` | integer | `0` | L-BFGS iterations after Adam (0: none) |
| `lr_adam` | number | `0.05` | Adam learning rate at the start |
| `lr_adam_end` | number | `0.002` | Adam learning rate at the end (cosine schedule) |
| `nested_init` | true/false | `true` | start each K from the K-1 fit with its heaviest population split |
| `kmeans_after_warm` | true/false | `true` | also start from k-means when the nested start is used |
| `split_delta` | number | `0.5` | logit shift between the halves of a split population |
| `warm_noise` | number | `0.05` | sd of the jitter added to a warm start |
| `grad_clip` | text | `"per_measurement"` | "per_measurement" (each fit on its own) or "global" gradient clipping |
| `polish_steps` | integer | `40` | Levenberg-Marquardt iterations per measurement after the restarts (0: none) |
| `seed` | integer | `0` | seed of everything random (each spectrum is also seeded by what it is: sample, peptide, charge, replicate, time, role) |
| `screen` | true/false | `false` | fit K > 1 only where it could be selected: about a third of the time, but the skipped fits are missing from fixed-K analyses (with [run.population_test]: only where the test could find it) |

## `[run.fit.noise]`

Noise model and level of the fit (hxex.noise.NoiseConfig). The level sets the loss scale and the model selection. Today's default is one sd per spectrum; estimate = "controls" gives every bin its own noise.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | text | `"gaussian"` | "gaussian" or "poisson" |
| `sd` | number or list | unset | gaussian: the sd in intensity units (false: percent instead) |
| `percent` | number | `3.0` | sd (or poisson scale) as percent of the tallest peak of the series' undeuterated reference spectrum |
| `n_eff` | number | unset | poisson: effective counts in the tallest peak (false: percent) |
| `estimate` | text | unset | "controls": every bin its own noise, measured from the undeuterated controls, plus model_error (opt-in; guide: The noise model); "replicates": estimate each series' noise from its replicate spectra (false: the level above) |
| `min_replicated` | integer | `3` | estimate: fewest time points with two or more replicates |
| `min_share` | number | `0.005` | estimate: smallest share of a spectrum's intensity a bin needs |
| `outlier_score` | number | `4.0` | estimate: a replicate scoring above this is left out and flagged noise_outlier |
| `model_error` | number | `9.0` | estimate = "controls": allowance for model error, percent of each bin's intensity; lower: smaller errors and more spectra split into populations, higher: larger errors and fewer |

## `[run.fit.backend]`

Where the fit runs (hxex.model.Backend); nothing is set globally.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | text | `"auto"` | "auto" (CUDA if available, else CPU), "cpu", "cuda" or "cuda:N" |
| `dtype` | text | `"auto"` | "auto" (float32), "float32" or "float64" (the last digits) |

## `[run.bootstrap]`

Standard errors and intervals from resampled refits of every measurement (hxex.bootstrap.BootstrapConfig). Slow: most of a run's time.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_boot` | integer | `20` | resamples of every measurement: 20 gives usable standard errors; raise it (100 or more) when the 95 % intervals matter |
| `ci` | number | `95.0` | interval width in percent (95.0), not a fraction |
| `n_restarts` | integer | `3` | starting points per refit (the first is the original fit) |
| `adam_steps` | integer | `400` | Adam steps per refit |
| `lr_adam` | number | `0.02` | Adam learning rate at the start of a refit |
| `lr_adam_end` | number | `0.002` | Adam learning rate at the end of a refit |
| `warm_noise` | number | `0.1` | sd of the jitter on the original fit |
| `polish_steps` | integer | `40` | Levenberg-Marquardt iterations per refit (0: none) |
| `grad_clip` | text | `"per_measurement"` | as in [run.fit] |
| `seed` | integer | `42` | seed of the resampling and the restarts |
| `keep_draws` | true/false | `false` | keep every resample's fit in the bundle |
| `curve_band` | true/false | `true` | also the band of the total uptake curve |
| `ks` | text or list | `"selected"` | "selected" (each measurement at its own K), "all" fitted K, or a list of K (fixed-K bootstraps for the analysis) |

## `[run.population_test]`

Tests how many populations each spectrum, and each set of replicates and charge states, holds against simulated spectra (hxex.population_test.PopulationTestConfig). Each spectrum's K is then the test's; needs k_min = 1. Slow: ten to twenty times the fit per step.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `simulations` | integer | `20` | simulated spectra per spectrum and step for the test's reference (20; time grows with it) |
| `significance` | number | `0.01` | a further population counts when the chance of seeing the evidence without it is below this |
| `min_population` | number | `0.1` | ... and the further population is at least this share of the molecules |
| `null` | text | `"simulated"` | "simulated", or "chi_square" for a quick first look without simulations (less exact) |
| `seed` | integer | `0` | seed of the simulations |

## `[run.controls]`

Back-exchange correction from the undeuterated and fully deuterated controls, fitted at K=1 (hxex.controls.ControlConfig). Deuterium retention here is the fraction of deuterium kept, not a retention time.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `undeut_at` | number | unset | s (or "5 min"): the spectra at this time also serve as the undeuterated control (false: only the files marked undeut) |
| `fulldeut_at` | number | unset | s (or "20 h"): the spectra at this time also serve as the fully deuterated control, e.g. a plateaued late time point (false: only the files marked fulldeut) |
| `undeut_marked` | true/false | `true` | the files marked undeut serve as the control (false: only the spectra at undeut_at do) |
| `fulldeut_marked` | true/false | `true` | the files marked fulldeut serve as the control (false: only the spectra at fulldeut_at do, e.g. when the measured file reads low) |
| `m0_max` | number | `0.5` | largest mean (D) of a good undeuterated control |
| `retention_min` | number | unset | a fixed smallest deuterium retention of a good fully deuterated control, as a fraction (false: none; the controls are judged against the run, outlier_sd, or the kint prediction); not a retention time |
| `retention_max` | number | `1.1` | largest deuterium retention of a good fully deuterated control, as a fraction |
| `outlier_sd` | number | `4.0` | a fully deuterated control this many robust standard deviations below the median retention of the run's controls is rejected (without retention_min) |
| `time_course_tolerance` | number | `0.1` | D per amide: a fully deuterated control below its series' highest time point by more than this is rejected (an undeuterated one above its lowest is flagged data_below_m0) |
| `sample_tolerance` | number | `0.1` | a fully deuterated control whose retention differs this much from the same peptide's in the other samples is flagged fd_disagrees (still used) |
| `combine_charges` | true/false | `true` | every charge state of a peptide (in one sample) takes the mean retention of its measured fully deuterated controls over all charge states; fd_fallback only when none is good (peptides only, not fragment ions) |
| `fd_other_charge` | true/false | `true` | with combine_charges = false: a series without a good fully deuterated control takes the retention of the same peptide's at its other charge states, before fd_fallback |
| `fd_other_sample` | true/false | `true` | a series without a good fully deuterated control at any charge takes the same peptide's retention in the run's other samples (fd_other_sample), before the retention map and fd_fallback |
| `fd_retention_map` | true/false | `true` | next, the retention of the overlapping peptides with good controls, fitted residue by residue (fd_map), before fd_fallback; needs peptide positions |
| `deamidation` | true/false | `false` | fully deuterated controls heated near neutral pH: where a sample's Asn-Gly peptides read deamidated (from the peaks' m/z), lower their controls by the share (fd_deamidated) |
| `deamidation_min_share` | number | `0.25` | the deamidated share (0 to 1) from which a sample's Asn-Gly controls are corrected |
| `replicate_outlier` | number | `6.0` | a control replicate this many typical replicate sd from its replicates' median (three or more) is left out of the control's mean (one above the amide count always is); unset: off |
| `d2o_fraction` | number | `0.9` | D atom fraction of the labelling buffer (0 to 1); [analysis.controls] may change it for the analysis |
| `fd_fallback` | text | unset | retention of a series without a good fully deuterated control: "d2o" (d2o_fraction), "median" (of the run's accepted controls) or "kint" (predicted back-exchange; needs quench; series it cannot predict take the median); false: "kint" with quench, else "median" |
| `quench` | table | unset | pH read, degrees Celsius and D fraction of the quench and LC ({ ph_read = 2.5, temperature = 0.0, d2o_fraction = 0.0 }), for fd_fallback "kint" (unset: none) |
| `kint_tolerance` | number | `0.15` | kint: a measured control this far (D per amide) from the prediction is rejected |
| `kint_min_series` | integer | `10` | kint: fewest usable controls to fit the prediction to (fewer: every series takes the median) |

## `[run.quality]`

Quality flags on every spectrum (hxex.quality.QualityConfig): poor_fit, low_intensity, noise_outlier, mz_shift, off_mz (thresholds in [run.picker]), poor_envelope, saturated, tails_low, bright. Nothing is dropped; the review layer of the bundle takes the decisions.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `poor_fit_factor` | number | `10.0` | poor_fit: misfit this many times the series' median |
| `min_deviance` | number | `1.0` | poor_fit: and a reduced deviance above this |
| `min_series_fits` | integer | `5` | poor_fit: fewest fitted spectra in a series to judge |
| `min_intensity` | number | `0.3` | low_intensity: total intensity below this share of the other replicates' mean |
| `max_mz_offset_ppm` | number | `15.0` | mz_shift: a series' m/z offset (ppm) beyond this, for series [run.picker] off_mz_sd does not check (fragment ions; false: screen off) |
| `saturated_ratio` | number | `1.15` | saturated: an undeuterated control whose peaks beside the tallest read above this times natural abundance (false: off) |
| `tails_low_ratio` | number | `0.7` | tails_low: an undeuterated control whose tail peaks (1-10 % of the top) read below this times natural abundance (false: off) |

## `[run.registry]`

Modified residues, written in sequences as modX labels (a lowercase prefix plus the residue letter, e.g. acK, pS; a sequence is read residue by residue). Each [[run.registry.residues]] adds delta to the base residue's composition. The table itself stays empty.


## `[[run.registry.residues]]`

One table per modified residue; the default registry holds acK, pS, pT and pY.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | text | required | the modX label used in sequences ("pS": a lowercase prefix plus the residue letter) |
| `base` | text | required | the standard residue it modifies |
| `delta` | table | required | composition added to the base residue ({ H = 1, P = 1, O = 3 }) |

## `[run.envelope]`

The isotope envelope that places the bins and shapes the fit (hxex.picking.EnvelopeConfig). Fragment spectra can hold several ion types of one fragment a hydrogen apart (c-1, c, c+1 in ETD).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | text | `"theory"` | "theory" (the ion type's isotope clusters), "mixed" (ion types a hydrogen apart, weights fitted to the undeuterated spectra) or "infer" (the undeuterated envelope itself) |
| `components` | integer | `2` | mixed: number of ion types |
| `max_residual` | number | `0.15` | largest relative residual of a mixture that describes its references (else poor_envelope) |
| `iterations` | integer | `3` | rounds of picking and fitting the weights |
| `share` | true/false | `false` | conditions of one ion that differ only in scan filters or label share an envelope |

## `[review]`

Decisions made after looking at the results: the user review table and the exclusion rules below. hxex run (its tables), hxex report and hxex analyse, given the project file, all apply them; the fits stay in the bundle. See [Reviewing results](project-file.md#reviewing-results).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | path | unset | the user review table: a copy of spectra.csv with review_status (rejected or accepted), review_K (the number of populations to use), and note filled in; other columns are ignored. Any name (the guide suggests "user_review_table.csv"); a name alone is a file beside the project file |

## `[[review.exclude]]`

Spectra treated as rejected, in the tables, figures, and analysis; their fits stay in the bundle. The same keys as [[input.exclude]]. (Called [[analysis.exclude]] before; that name still works.) See [Excluding spectra](excluding-spectra.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sample` | text | unset | the sample |
| `peptide_range` | text | unset | the peptide, by its residues ("45-60" is "0045-0060") |
| `charge` | integer | unset | the charge state |
| `time` | number or text | unset | a time point (s, or text with a unit: "30 s"); a control has no time |
| `role` | text | unset | "undeut" or "fulldeut": the controls |
| `rep` | integer | unset | the replicate |
| `file` | text | unset | the data file's name: a run's mzML or raw file, an HX-Express spreadsheet, or a SpecExport spectrum file |
| `spectrum_id` | text | unset | one spectrum, by its id (spectra.csv) |
| `note` | text | `""` | why: kept with the record, and shown by hxex check and hxex info |

## `[analysis]`

The post-fitting analysis that `hxex analyse` writes (`hxex.analysis`). See docs/ANALYSIS.md for the methods.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reference` | text | `""` | the sample the others are compared with (empty: no comparisons); `"run:sample"` names one run's sample |
| `samples` | list | `[]` | which samples, in this order (empty: all, the reference first) |
| `times` | list | `[]` | time points of the per-time figures (empty: all) |
| `exclude_times` | list | `[]` | time points left out of the whole analysis (unreliable ones; the fits are kept) |
| `ks` | list | `[1, 2]` | the fixed K values analysed (1 is needed) |
| `fasta` | text or table | unset | one sequence file for every sample, or a table of sample = file (a run's own under its name); unset: the sequence comes from the peptides |
| `coverage_times` | text or list | `"undeuterated"` | "undeuterated" (judged on the undeuterated controls), "all", or a list of times |
| `redundancy` | text | `"peptides"` | what the redundancy counts: "peptides" or "spectra" |
| `weight_exponent` | number | `1.0` | exponent of the residue averaging's weights |
| `alpha` | number | `0.05` | significance level of the comparisons |
| `exclude_flagged` | true/false | `false` | leave out spectra with a quality flag |
| `format` | text | `"pdf"` | of the figure files: "pdf", "png" or "svg" |
| `out` | text | unset | the output directory (unset: beside the bundle, named after it and the reference: results_analysis_WT, or results_analysis without a reference) |
| `overlay` | list | `["low", "high", "avg"]` | the values of the by-residue comparisons: "low" and "high" (the K=2 populations' fD), "avg" (K=1), and/or "pop_low", "pop_high" (the populations' shares) |
| `overlay_two_only` | true/false | `true` | draw K=2 values only where the choice keeps two populations |
| `peptide_match` | text | `"range"` | which peptides are compared: "range" (the same residues, mutated or not) or "sequence" (identical sequences) |
| `populations` | text | unset | how the number of populations is decided: "population_test" (the population test of each peptide's spectra together, made by [run.population_test]; the default when the run has it), "best_set" (where a peptide's spectra together are best described by two; a residue where such peptides carry half its weight; K=2 compared where both samples have two; the default without the test) or "bootstrap" (the residue's K=2 positions and their bootstrap errors, with [analysis.choice]'s limits) |
| `borderline_evidence` | number | `10.0` | where the number of populations differs between samples: borderline unless the two-population side's summed criterion is at least this far below 0 and the other's above 0 (with populations = "population_test" the test's p-values decide instead: below significance / 10 on the side with more populations, above significance x 10 on the other) |
| `modified_peptides` | text | `"separate"` | "separate" (modified forms as states of their own) or "combined" (averaged with the sample) |
| `protection` | true/false | `false` | opt in to the peptides' protection factors (needs [analysis.labelling]) |

## `[analysis.filters]`

Which spectra and K=2 descriptions the analysis trusts. Whole spectra: spectrum_quality_filtering, replicate_outlier, above_amides, stand_in_controls (the spectra left out are listed in left_out_spectra.csv; one you accept in the review is kept). K=2 descriptions per spectrum: min_population, max_fD; per species and time: max_fD_se, k1_between_ranks.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_population` | number | `0.05` | every population of a spectrum within [min_population, 1 - min_population] |
| `max_fD_se` | number | `0.25` | every population's fD standard error below this |
| `max_fD` | number | `1.1` | no population deuterated beyond this fraction of the amides (with the population test, such a spectrum also leaves the test, at one population) |
| `k1_between_ranks` | true/false | `true` | the K=1 value lies between the two populations' values |
| `replicate_outlier` | number | `6.0` | leave out a spectrum whose K=1 fD lies more than this many typical replicate standard deviations from the median of its replicates (same charge state, three or more); unset: off |
| `above_amides` | true/false | `true` | leave out a spectrum whose K=1 mean exceeds the amide count before the back-exchange correction |
| `stand_in_controls` | text | `"exclude"` | "exclude" or "include" the series whose fully deuterated control is a stand-in (a sample with no measured control keeps them) or whose undeuterated control read above [run.controls] m0_max (m0_high: another species); "other_sample" excludes them but keeps the series that took the same peptide's control in another sample |
| `spectrum_quality_filtering` | text | `"loose"` | "loose", "strict", or "none": what the spectrum quality screens do: leave out spectra showing another species, keep one population only, or warn (fragments are not screened) |
| `undeuterated_cap` | true/false | `false` | with the population test: keep the other spectra of a peptide whose undeuterated set has two populations or more at one population, in every sample (off: the peptide is only flagged, undeuterated_two) |

## `[analysis.choice]`

The limits of the choice between one and two populations. With populations = "bootstrap" they are the rule itself, so their defaults are strict (0.95, 10 %); with "best_set" they only check the result of the fits' comparison (0.5, 5 %). A key you set applies in either mode. A residue whose K=2 standard errors are unknown keeps the one-population description.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confidence` | number | `0.5` | a fraction (0.5: 50 %): the interval that must separate the two K=2 values; default 0.5 with populations = "best_set", 0.95 with "bootstrap" |
| `max_fD_se` | number | `0.25` | both K=2 standard errors below this |
| `min_population` | number | `0.05` | the low-D population (lever rule) within [min_population, 1 - min_population]; default 0.05 with populations = "best_set", 0.10 with "bootstrap" |
| `tier` | text | `"two"` | with populations = "population_test": the least residue tier with two populations, "two" (strong evidence and a third of the covering weight agrees) or "localised" (half); the other limits of this table do not apply then |

## `[analysis.controls]`

Any key of [run.controls]; the controls are then recomputed from the run's K=1 fits.


## `[analysis.runs]`

Separate runs to compare: run name = bundle path (default: this project's bundle). The tables then get a run column.


## `[analysis.merge]`

Samples combined across runs: `"run:sample" = label`; the same label pools them (fragment series are drawn side by side, not pooled).


## `[[analysis.regions]]`

Repeat the table for every region (regions may overlap).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | required | the region's name |
| `start` | integer | required | first residue (1-based, inclusive) |
| `end` | integer | required | last residue (inclusive) |

## `[[analysis.sites]]`

Repeat the table for every site (a modification, a mutation).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `residue` | integer | required | the residue number |
| `label` | text | `""` | the label drawn ("S19") |

## `[analysis.fragments]`

The fragment outputs of a run with fragment series (ladders, rates, closure, per-residue rates); written whenever the run has fragments.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ion_types` | list | `[]` | the fragment ion types analysed (empty: every one of the run) |
| `charges` | list | `[1]` | the fragment charges analysed |
| `min_time` | number | unset | s on the exchange clock: earlier points are drawn but not fitted (not [input.scans] min_time, on the scan clock) |
| `tolerance` | number | `0.25` | deuterons: a closure c + z - M beyond this is flagged |
| `precursor_charge` | integer | unset | the closure's precursor charge (unset: the unreacted precursor) |
| `max_rate_error` | number | `0.5` | ladder steps with rate_se / rate at most this give the per-residue rates (ladder_residues.csv) |
| `kint` | true/false | `false` | opt in: intrinsic rates, protection factors and theoretical curves (needs [analysis.fragments.exchange]) |

## `[analysis.fragments.labels]`

Short condition names: condition = name ("gentle" = "G"), or a run's own under its name ([analysis.fragments.labels.RUN]).


## `[analysis.fragments.exchange]`

The solvent the fragment kinetics happen in, for every sample, or one table per sample ([analysis.fragments.exchange.SAMPLE]) or per run and sample. Its d2o_fraction is the kinetics' solvent, not the labelling buffer's.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ph_read` | number | required | the pH meter reading in the solvent (glass electrode, uncorrected) |
| `temperature` | number | required | degrees Celsius |
| `d2o_fraction` | number | required | deuterium atom fraction of the solvent, 0 to 1 |
| `reference` | text | `"PDLA"` | intrinsic-rate set: "PDLA" (poly-DL-alanine) or "3Ala" |
| `factors` | table | {} | log10 Bai factors [AL, AR, BL, BR] for modified residues (label = list), replacing those of their standard residue |
| `initial_fraction` | number | unset | D fraction of the amides when the exchange began (the start of the theoretical curves; unset: no curves) |

## `[analysis.labelling]`

The labelling solvent of the peptide protection factors, for every sample, or one table per sample ([analysis.labelling.SAMPLE]) or per run and sample.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ph_read` | number | required | the pH meter reading in the solvent (glass electrode, uncorrected) |
| `temperature` | number | required | degrees Celsius |
| `d2o_fraction` | number | required | deuterium atom fraction of the solvent, 0 to 1 |
| `reference` | text | `"PDLA"` | intrinsic-rate set: "PDLA" (poly-DL-alanine) or "3Ala" |
| `factors` | table | {} | log10 Bai factors [AL, AR, BL, BR] for modified residues (label = list), replacing those of their standard residue |
| `initial_fraction` | number | unset | back-exchange only: the D fraction the amides began with (above d2o_fraction: fD falls with time); leave it out for labelling |

## `[figures]`

Figures, drawn by hxex report hxex.toml --figures from the results (hxex run draws none; hxex.report.PlotConfig). Changing these needs no new run. See [Outputs](outputs.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | text or list | `"flagged"` | "flagged" (series with a flag, a rejection or a control fallback), "all" or a list of data_id |
| `kinds` | list | `["spectra", "populations", "uptake"]` | pages of a series' figure: spectra, populations, uptake |
| `show` | list | `["raw", "picked", "fit"]` | layers of the spectra page: raw, picked, fit |
| `x` | text | unset | uptake axis: "time" or "index" (unset: "time", or "index" when the times only order the points, input.time_scale = "order") |
| `scale` | text | `"linear"` | uptake axis: "linear" or "log" |
| `corrected` | true/false | unset | draw back-exchange corrected values (unset: when there are controls; a series without correction, such as a fragment ion, is drawn as measured) |
| `format` | text | `"pdf"` | "pdf" (one file per series, a page per kind), "png" or "svg" (one file per kind) |
| `dpi` | integer | `300` | resolution of PNG files and of raster images in PDF or SVG |
| `overview` | true/false | `true` | also the run's overview (K selection, controls, quality flags) |
| `residual` | true/false | `false` | a residual panel under every spectrum |
| `k` | integer | unset | draw every series at this number of populations (unset: each spectrum at its own K, the fit's or the review's choice) |
